channel.title: EU & Swiss News - Economy, Politics, Security
channel.description: Premium curated news on EU and Swiss economy, politics, and security from top international sources

item.title: [DW Security] Finland: Google announces €13 billion AI, energy investment
item.description: Google has announced a plan to expand AI data centers and buy massive amounts of nuclear energy. Finland's security services have warned of there are risks, but the right-wing government says the deal will bring jobs.

item.title: [DW Security] Norway's PM: Zelenskyy's plane almost hit by drone
item.description: A drone nearly struck a plane carrying Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy from Moldova to Oslo, according to Norway's prime minister. However, a Ukrainian source said the threat may have been overstated.

item.title: [DW Europe] Putin rejects mobilization rumors, many Russians unconvinced
item.description: Russia’s President Vladimir Putin has dismissed rumors about military mobilization. But many Russians, including many DW users, say they are preparing for the possibility.

item.title: [European Council on Foreign Relations] A future with Chinese characteristics
item.description: The world is undergoing a historical and cultural rupture. Just as Hollywood and other American exports once gave the rest of the world a glimpse of modern life and the future that awaited them, China is now doing the same for African, Latin American and even American young people

item.title: [European Council on Foreign Relations] Friends without benefits: Why the EU should offer Canada more than casual defence ties
item.description: Trump is pushing Canada—a quiet military powerhouse—away from America. The EU should seize the chance and fold it into its own defence

item.title: [DW Europe] German economy frets about Saxony-Anhalt election results
item.description: The AfD won the election in the eastern German state by a wide margin. While politicians and election analysts are still debating the reasons for the far-right party's popularity, economists are sounding the alarm.

item.title: [DW Europe] Ratko Mladic’s funeral casts shadow over Bosnia and Herzegovina vote
item.description: Ratko Mladic’s funeral in Belgrade, attended by Serbian and Bosnian Serb leaders, has deepened regional tensions and could affect the upcoming election in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

item.title: [European Council on Foreign Relations] Future nostalgia: Europe’s unfinished song
item.description: ECFR’s new research reveals Europeans are suffering from an imagination gap. Many people want to see Europe strong and flourishing—but fewer can picture a credible route from today’s disruptions to that destination

item.title: [European Council on Foreign Relations] Beyond Saxony-Anhalt: What Merz’s crisis means for Europe
item.description: The far-right AfD’s win in a small German state calls for dynamism in Berlin and hedging in Brussels

item.title: [European Council on Foreign Relations] Emergency Room: The AfD’s victory in Saxony-Anhalt
item.description: Mark Leonard welcomes Jana Puglierin, senior policy fellow and head of ECFR’s Berlin office, to discuss the Alternative for Germany (AfD)’s election win in Saxony-Anhalt—and what it means for Germany and Europe

item.title: [European Council on Foreign Relations] Britons back ban on trade with Israeli settlements by more than two to one
item.description: New polling published by ECFR shows that Britons across the political divide favour banning trade with illegal Israeli settlements

item.title: [DW Security] Ecuador: Ex-president Bucaram sentenced in corruption case
item.description: Abdala Bucaram, Ecuador's former president, was convicted of organized crime for his role in the illegal sale of COVID-19 tests and medical supplies, receiving a prison sentence of over nine years.

item.title: [DW Security] Germany: Energy boss urges better infrastructure protection
item.description: The chief of power giant RWE says Germany's rules for protecting vital infrastructure are outdated, calling for greater secrecy. Meanwhile, German inflation rose as the ECB consideres interest rates. DW has the latest.

item.description: Having spent the summer trying to ease the cost of living, is a new tourist tax about to hit domestic holiday makers in the pocket? item.title: [DW Europe] Serbia, the conflicted EU candidate
item.description: On paper, Belgrade has pursued EU membership for years. But accession has long been stalled. The hero's farewell given to war criminal Mladic exposed just how far Serbia has alienated itself from Europe.

item.title: [DW Security] August hottest month ever recorded, says EU monitor
item.description: The average global temperature in August broke the previous record set in 2023. Climate scientists say record summer heat in the northern hemisphere and warmer oceans are all part of a new normal.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Why the US is staying so measured about allies’ sanctions on Israeli settlements
item.description: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee “is totally out on his own” with his threats against the U.K., as most of the Trump administration treads carefully.

item.description: The U.S. is on a public campaign to dismantle the International Criminal Court. Now, it wants help from its NATO allies.  During a closed-door meeting back in July, U.S. envoy to NATO Matthew Whitaker asked allied countries for help in disassembling the international court that addresses genocide and crimes against humanity.  On the show, Sarah Wheaton and Kathryn […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] Trump pledges a $5,000 ‘dividend’ to all US adults if the GOP wins the midterms
item.description: It was not immediately clear how the plan would be financed.

item.title: [Politico Europe] ‘A communist caucus’: Trump gives Republicans their midterms enemy
item.description: Trump, on the first night of the whirlwind two-day convention, warned of a “communist” takeover he said would destroy the nation.

item.title: [DW Security] Trump promises Americans $5,000 if Republicans win midterms
item.description: The US president gave a wide-ranging speech at the Republican midterm convention. He defended the war in Iran, trade wars and tariffs, and the White House ballroom. He also called Democrats evil and immigrants animals.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Mobility: Europe must move from targets to the conditions for delivering them
item.description: It is one thing to set goals; you also need to create the economic and political conditions to realize them.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Zelenskyy’s big bet: Ukraine can outlast Russia
item.description: Deep strikes inside Russia aim to raise pressure on Vladimir Putin as Kyiv braces for another punishing winter.

item.title: [DW Security] Philippines: Several killed, dozens missing after fire on ferry
item.description: Footage released by the Coast Guard showed the vessel engulfed in flames as rescuers brought bodies ashore in body bags. The ship's manifest listed 134 passengers and crew.

item.title: [DW Europe] US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold Ukraine talks after meeting Putin
item.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv, seeking to revive efforts to end the war. But the latest diplomatic push seems to have produced no breakthrough.

item.title: [DW Europe] Germany, Kosovo unite against ticks carrying deadly virus
item.description: Germany has high-security labs while Kosovo has Hyalomma ticks and experience with the deadly Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever. Working together, German and Kosovar scientists are fighting the disease and its vectors.

item.title: [DW Europe] Hungary begins hunt for corrupt regime's billions
item.description: Hungary's new prime minister promised he would recover billions stolen or diverted by the previous administration. A new "super authority" is about to begin that work. Its success or failure will have a big impact.

item.title: [DW Europe] War criminal Ratko Mladic buried with military honors in Belgrade, Serbia
item.description: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb commander convicted of genocide in Srebrenica, has been buried in Belgrade. The funeral, broadcast live on TV, comes just days before President Vucic is expected to call an election.

item.title: [European Council on Foreign Relations] Against war, drought and hunger: A global coalition to prevent a food crisis
item.description: Three features of today’s unordered world are converging to create a devastating food crisis. Russia’s war in Ukraine is disrupting agricultural exports from both countries. item.title: [European Council on Foreign Relations] Orchestrators, not customers: A new role for European governments in defence
item.description: Weapons that took decades to develop can now be countered within months. European governments need to stop buying finished platforms and start running an innovation cycle, in which soldiers learn from one system and build these lessons into the next
